title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defense
line: Black holds the center with pawns, and White aims a rook down the c-file.

steps.text: Black holds the center pawn with another pawn and brings out its pieces. Its bishop on c8 is shut in behind the pawn on e6.
Move the pawn in front of your king one square. It guards your center pawn and frees your other bishop.
Bring out your other knight. It guards your center pawn too.
steps.after: This is the Orthodox Defense, the oldest main line of the Queen's Gambit.

steps.text: Put a rook behind the pawn on c4. When the pawns there trade, the file opens for your rook.

also.d1c2: That is another main line. This lesson puts the rook on the file first.

steps.after: Black adds a pawn to guard the center and waits.

steps.text: Bring out the last bishop toward Black's king.
steps.after: Black waited to take on c4 until your bishop had moved. Now the bishop spends a second move to take back.

steps.text: Take the pawn back with the bishop. Material is level again.
steps.after: Black's knight jumps to the center to trade pieces and free its game.

steps.text: The knight has left f6, so the bishops face each other. Trade on e7.
Castle. Your rook already stands on the c-file, where White has no pawn.
steps.after: White's minor pieces are out and the king is safe. Black still has to free the bishop on c8.

summary: Black holds the center with pawns and a shut in bishop. White develops everything and puts a rook on the c-file.
